title: Senate stalls bill over power-grid costs for the US digital economy
key_facts: The Ratepayer Protection Act failed to advance in the Senate: 57 for, 43 against, below the 60 votes required.
Backers: Senator Jon Husted (R-Ohio), Reps. Gabe Evans (R-Colo.) and Kathy Castor (D-Fla.).
It would have state regulators and certain utilities weigh standards making facilities of at least 100 MW peak demand responsible for the full extra costs of generation and grid upgrades.
States would keep the power to adopt it or not.
The source is a CoinDesk column of 14 Oct 2026 by Rashan Colbert, director of US policy at the Crypto Council for Innovation.
quote_evidence: The procedural vote drew 57 supporters and 43 opponents, below the 60 votes required to move the measure forward.
The proposal would leave adoption authority with states.
why_it_matters_hint: Who pays for grid upgrades for data centers is unresolved.
